newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alestra phone service ready in two Mexican cities.
newsitem.headline: Alestra phone service ready in two Mexican cities.

text.p: Mexican telephone company Alestra said on Tuesday it will be ready to offer telephone service in the cities of Queretaro and Monterrey on Jan. 1 and 10, respectively.

Alestra, a joint venture between U.S. phone giant AT&T, Mexican holding company VISA-Bancomer and industrial firm Alfa, said that by the end of this month, it will have installed 4,300 kilometers of high-speed fiber-optic cable.
The company also said it had successfully finished interconnection tests that link its network in 24 different cities to that of former monopoly Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex).

Alestra officials said they expect to get 60 percent of their business from corporate clients and about 40 percent from residential customers, eventually poaching enough disgruntled clients from Telmex to gain a dominant market position.
"We believe that in five years, we will be the single largest provider of long-distance in Mexico," Alestra spokesman Jorge Escribano said at a news conference.
By the end of this year, Alestra will have invested $450 million in setting up its long-distance network. It plans to invest a total of $1 billion by the year 2000.
Officials said Alestra began distributing forms in Monterrey on Monday that allow potential customers to pre-select Alestra for their long-distance carrier beginning Jan. 1.
The company said in a separate statement that its fiber-optic cable can carry 20 gigabytes of information per second. It added that its digital switchboard equipment is also state-of-the-art.
Alestra will be competing primarily with Telmex and Avantel, a joint venture between MCI Communications Corp. and Mexico's Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival.
